body.statement: Using the handle \(\mathsf H_B\), establish \(U(G_n,k_n)\le C_U r(n,d_n)\) with probability tending to one for every admissible degree sequence. One sufficient route is to prove that a universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies \[\Pr\!\left\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}\longrightarrow1;\] if that norm statement is false, derive the certificate bound directly from the centered collision expansion without assuming a favorable rate.
body.justification: This is the sole exposed frontier step: Booleanization, not adjacency spectral control, must save a polynomial factor in the two-arm covariance.
body.gap: Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Section 2.2, Theorems 14--15, controls polynomial graph matrices, and BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity controls adjacency powers, but Boolean radius-two reachability includes nonlinear collision corrections and the required uniform constant-to-near-square-root degree splice is absent.
body.consumer: A positive solution certifies the attaining design at the lower-bound rate; a negative solution kills the sampler spine before a false minimax theorem is claimed.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove uniformly over \(3\le d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) that \(U(G_n,k_n)=O_{\Pr}(r(n,d_n))\), or prove the sufficient estimate \(\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\Pr}(d_n^{7/4})\).
obligation.obstruction: Adjacency spectral control bounds \((A_G^2+A_G-(d_n-1)I_n)P_n\), but it does not bound the centered Boolean collision correction. Its uncentered row mass can be of order \(d_n^4/n\) near the upper degree boundary, while Frobenius and maximum-row bounds lose the required power. The available fixed-polynomial graph-matrix theorem does not directly control the unbounded inclusion-exclusion expansion of the Boolean threshold uniformly down to slowly growing degree.
obligation.attempted: Expanded the correction into triangle and repeated-codegree terms; tested Frobenius, maximum-row, and Schur-covariance routes; and ran the requested Boolean-spectrum and actual-certificate grid through degrees close to \(\sqrt n\). None supplies the required uniform trace-moment estimate, while the finite grid does not refute it.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact deterministic reduction is
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]
\le U(G,k_n).
\]
Moreover, if \(\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\Pr}(d_n^{7/4})\), then the definition of \(k_n\), \(-\log(1-x)\asymp x\) for \(x=d_n^2/n=o(1)\), and the displayed formula for \(U\) give \(U(G_n,k_n)=O_{\Pr}\{d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\}\).  On girth-at-least-five graphs the identity \(B_2=A_G^2+A_G-(d_n-1)I_n\) reduces the norm to \(O(d_n)\) whenever \(\|A_GP_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(\sqrt{d_n})\).  Exact finite enumeration validates the covariance identity.  A separate numerical falsification grid with \(2000\le n\le12000\), \(3\le d\le70\), including \(d^2/n\) up to \(0.408\), found \(\|B_2P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}/d\) between \(2.19\) and \(3.21\) and \(U/r\) between \(8.71\) and \(12.62\); this does not prove the asymptotic assertion.
